classification: executable acceptance plan, no executed tests or review verdict
production_fixture_requirement: serve actual A2aServer::router over real TcpListener; handwritten existing client wire server and router.call tests are supporting baselines only
policy_backend_fixture_scope: controlled host policy and owned instrumented stream measure library guard; not a real IdP/durable backend/external consumer/pilot

oracles.setup_action: Observe SubscribeToTask and SendStreamingMessage with the flag omitted
oracles.required_observation: Only the original prepare authorization/admission runs; no new recheck/poll/order/error/timeout behavior is introduced

oracles.setup_action: Apply no-arg enable twice; clone; compose before/after with_timeouts/with_limits
oracles.required_observation: Enable is idempotent and Clone preserves it; original numerical limits stay exact; flag advertises no streaming capability

oracles.setup_action: Deliver snapshot, update, terminal; record every authorizer request and backend poll/drop
oracles.required_observation: Each recheck uses original exact tenant/identity/canonical scopes, SubscribeToTask, original task ID, configNone; wire events unchanged; last successful postcheck precedes each delivery

oracles.setup_action: Latch the next pre-poll check; revoke originaltask before permit; keep first HTTP body alive
oracles.required_observation: Zero backend poll for that step, zero next data event; fixed existence-hiding stream error; backend Drop once and operation permit reusable by a different still-authorized task

oracles.setup_action: Let precheck allow, block backend next, revoke, then make second event ready
oracles.required_observation: Prepared second event is never delivered; no later poll; backend Drop once and permit released; old yielded bytes are outside claim

oracles.setup_action: Return Unavailable at precheck and separately after an event was obtained
oracles.required_observation: No affected event delivery; safe existing authorization-unavailable mapping; backend/permit retirement occurs before returning terminal error

oracles.setup_action: Hold precheck and postcheck futures with original request_timeout shorter than idle
oracles.required_observation: Check future is dropped at min(request deadline,idle deadline); no affected event; no callback/task is spawned or detached; prompt resource release

oracles.setup_action: Make precheck, backend wait and postcheck each individually shorter than idle but sum longer
oracles.required_observation: One absolute idle deadline spans all phases without resets; idle error and resource release, no event after deadline

oracles.setup_action: Use deterministic step polling plus real TCP timing control for ready-at/after-deadline and simultaneous shutdown
oracles.required_observation: Post-await actual clock and shutdown checks prevent proceeding/handing event off once observed expired/cancelled; no preemption or zero-gap network promise

oracles.setup_action: EOF, backend error, permitted terminal event and event-count exhaustion
oracles.required_observation: EOF/error/limit retire before return; terminal event passes postcheck then retires before handoff; no live backend/permit in terminal state; event count unchanged

oracles.setup_action: Cancel shared shutdown while waiting in precheck, backend next, or postcheck
oracles.required_observation: Pending futures dropped, at most one existing safe shutdown error, no further event/poll; backend Drop and operation permit release once

oracles.setup_action: Receive first event then close the actual TCP connection while each phase is pending
oracles.required_observation: When HTTP stack observes disconnect and drops body/stream, backend Drop and healthy-task permit reuse observed within bounded test wait; no claim at caller local Drop instant

oracles.setup_action: Keep first response/connection object alive after observed terminal error, with max operations1
oracles.required_observation: Healthy distinct task succeeds without dropping/repolling first response; direct strict-stream single-poll oracle also proves handles gone before yielded Err, avoiding SDK eager-drop false proof

oracles.setup_action: Pause network consumption and retain buffered first bytes
oracles.required_observation: No unbounded queue/recheck task; existing idle semantics start only when adapter step is polled; no periodic wall-clock revocation SLO during unpolled/backpressured state

oracles.setup_action: Exercise SendStreamingMessage and ordinary unary operations
oracles.required_observation: Original single prepare authorization/admission and bounded stream implementation preserved; no subscription guard, writes/cancellation/retry unchanged

oracles.setup_action: Unauthenticated malformed body, forbidden opaque task, queued admission policy changes
oracles.required_observation: Original authenticate-before-body, authorize-before-backend/admit/permit order remains; denied resource existence hidden, zero forbidden backend dispatch

oracles.setup_action: Change current host mapping while backend is pending; record every callback tuple
oracles.required_observation: Guard keeps original principal/task/op instead of remapping to another tenant/resource; current host authorizer refuses stale authority; stream payload or routing metadata never supplies new authorization facts

common_resource_probe: maximum_in_flight_operations=1, concurrent requests>=2, first taskA revoked but healthy taskB authorized; first response retained; do not release it merely to make probe pass
drop_order_proof: Combine direct next-step single-poll resource ownership oracle with actual TCP Drop/permit-reuse observations; TCP receipt order alone cannot prove adapter before-yield ordering
timing: Keep original allowed with_timeouts limits (request>=10ms,idle>=1s); use controlled latches and monotonic timestamps; never extend production caps for green tests
